title: GridContext
description: `GET /v1/grid/context` - what ONS **planned** for a day beside what the grid **did**, hour by hour, for one subsystem. Neither half is a WattSteer number: the programme is ONS's `carga-energia-programada` and the programmed interchange is ONS's, the realisation is the settled energy balance, and the only arithmetic here is a subtraction between two ONS series of the same unit and the same grain. It exists so that the product's own forecast can be read against the two official series rather than beside them, which is the distinction a reviewer is entitled to see drawn. Every field is nullable with a stated reason, because a programme not yet published and a load of zero are different facts.

date.description: The local civil day these hours belong to, America/Sao_Paulo.

as_of.description: The vintage cut: what WattSteer had learned by this instant.

hours.description: In `valid_time` order. A day is 24 hours except across a DST change, which Brazil no longer observes but the grain still permits.

corridors.description: The interchange links this subsystem sits on, summed over the day. Orientation is canonical (`from < to`), so a positive verified figure is a flow from `from_subsystem` to `to_subsystem` whichever end asked.

programmed_load_mwh.description: ONS's day-ahead load programme for this hour. `null` where no programme was published for it, which is the ordinary state of a day whose D-1 has not arrived - not a zero.

observed_load_mwh.description: The settled load. `null` where the hour is not settled yet.

observed_net_exchange_mwh.description: Positive is export. The subsystem's net position across every corridor it sits on.

context_day.title: ContextDay
context_day.description: The day's three figures. `deviation_mwh` is `observed - programmed` and is `null` unless **both** sides cover the same hours, because a deviation computed over a partial overlap is a measurement of the overlap and reads as a measurement of the day.

deviation_unavailable_reason.description: Why there is no deviation. `partial_overlap` is the one worth naming: both series exist and they do not describe the same hours.

hours_compared.description: How many hours carry both a programme and a settlement. A deviation over few hours is a different claim from one over 24.

verified_mwh.description: Summed over the hours that settled. `null` where none did.

programmed_mwh.description: ONS's programmed interchange, summed over the same hours it was published for. `null` where the corridor has no programme - the column is nullable at source.
